target.title: docs: propose plugin-owned external verification approvals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External plugins sometimes need a user to complete a verifier-specific ceremony before a protected tool can continue. OpenClaw should own the approval, denial, expiry, and tool continuation, while the plugin owns the verifier and proof.

The first concrete user is the external AgentKit plugin:

- https://github.com/Guardiola31337/openclaw-agentkit
- https://clawhub.ai/guardiola31337/plugins/agentkit

## Why This Change Was Made

This RFC proposes one narrow external-verification route on a plugin-owned approval:

- `requireApproval.externalResolution` carries a verifier label and canonical allow decisions, defaulting to `allow-once`
- core derives the owner from plugin registration and rejects external resolution on caller-identified public request paths
- an authenticated, out-of-band approval action binds the exact plugin, approval, and decision and creates a host-issued attempt
- the owning plugin receives an in-process verifier handler, a text-only challenge presentation sink, and an attempt-scoped completion helper
- successful completion goes through the existing canonical first-answer ledger; denial, expiry, cancellation, and competing terminal decisions still win
- verification start/end metadata is audited without storing proofs or verifier-specific private data in core
- unsupported hosts reject plugin registration, while clients without richer presentation fail closed with canonical command text and Deny

This does **not** add arbitrary plugin actions, a public plugin resolver RPC, `operator.admin` authority, World-specific core code, or new auto-review authority.

## User Impact

If accepted and implemented, a user can choose **Verify once**, **Verify and trust for session**, or **Deny** from the normal OpenClaw approval flow. The plugin can show its QR/link and attest successful verification, but only OpenClaw can commit the terminal decision. The verifier challenge is delivered while the agent run is blocked, and the original tool continues only after the owning plugin attests success through OpenClaw's canonical approval state machine.

The reference implementation is AgentKit:

- https://github.com/Guardiola31337/openclaw-agentkit
- https://clawhub.ai/guardiola31337/plugins/agentkit

## Evidence

Document validation:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- branch includes current `openclaw/rfcs` `main` (`2d213ae23462`)
- contract reviewed against current OpenClaw approval ownership, decision enum, canonical ledger, and plugin API boundaries
- independent security/API review findings incorporated for exact dispatch binding, out-of-band delivery, attempt-specific proof binding, response-loss replay, and grant idempotency

The RFC includes host contract tests, AgentKit integration tests, and a manual user-flow artifact as implementation acceptance criteria. Current OpenClaw `main` does not implement this API, so runtime proof belongs to the implementation PR and updated AgentKit release rather than being claimed by this document-only proposal.

Related implementation context:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82336
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78583
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82434
